Table 1 Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics. Characteristic Probiotic Group (n=170) Placebo Group (n=170) Age Groups (n;%) 18-30 years 25 (14.71) 30 (17.65) 31-45 years 50 (29.41) 45 (26.47) 46-60 years 60 (35.29) 55 (32.35) 61+ years 35 (20.59) 40 (23.53) (mean ± SD) 45.2 ± 15.4 46.1 ± 14.8 Gender (n;%) Male 87 (51.18) 81 (47.65) Female 83 (48.82) 89 (52.35) Underlying Conditions (n;%) Respiratory Infection 50 (29.41) 55 (32.35) Urinary Tract Infection 45 (26.47) 40 (23.53) Skin Infection 35 (20.59) 30 (17.65) Others 40 (23.53) 45 (26.47) Type of Antibiotics (n;%) Penicillin 50 (29.41) 55 (32.35) Cephalosporin 60 (35.29) 65 (38.24) Macrolides 25 (14.71) 30 (17.65) Fluoroquinolones 35 (20.59) 20 (11.76) In the probiotic group, 31 out of 170 patients (18.23%) developed AAD. In contrast, the placebo group had 53 out of 170 patients (31.17%) who experienced AAD (Figure 1 ). Figure 1 Incidence of antibiotic-associated diarrhea.
